reads_before_this_plan: STUDY_PLAN.md; the original follow-up code, plan and published result (followup_verification.py/.json, receipts/followup_verification_plan.json, REPORT.md section 6); jaaks.py, study.py, verdict.py; direction_exploration_20261003_v2/REPORT.md; Screening_documentation.pdf (pdftotext); a design-only probe of the Jaaks release (DESIGN_COLUMNS via the frozen jaaks._read: no outcome column, no ticket) giving 296,707 rows, one row per (plate, anchor, anchor concentration, library drug), 3,106 plates, one line per plate, about 25 anchors and 2 library drugs per plate, 1-10 design plates per line x orientation (46 lines have some orientation on more than one plate).
status: EXPLORATORY. Jaaks et al. 2022 (figshare 16843597, SHA-256 1188968c...a278) was already opened by feedback_validation_20261003. Nothing here is confirmation; no verdict category is assigned.
question: When the budget is conserved (every arm spends its full feasible budget), final-round screen hits get a verification opportunity, and resources are charged by branch in physical units, how do screening-versus-verification schedulers compare in independently confirmed discoveries actually obtained through paid observations?
estimand: Per cell line: confirmed discoveries = pairs whose screen orientation was purchased and called synergistic AND whose other orientation (same pair, same line, disjoint plates) was purchased and called synergistic. Line value = mean over the SV and VS swap replicates (and over random seeds for random arms). Arm total = sum over 125 lines. Contrasts are paired line differences.

units.inference_unit: cell line (125 expected: 51 breast, 45 colon, 29 pancreas), stratified by tissue
units.not_independent: SV/VS replicates, plates, seeds and orientations are averaged within line, never counted as units

data_access.outcomes: only via common.exposed_ticket(purpose, 'allocation') then the frozen jaaks.build_panels(ticket, JAAKS); one ticket per execution of replay.py
data_access.design: design columns (BARCODE, SIDM, ANCHOR_ID, ANCHOR_CONC, LIBRARY_ID ...) via the frozen jaaks._read(JAAKS, DESIGN_COLUMNS) for plate counts, barcodes and native-plate composition (no outcome column)
data_access.orientation_mapping: row i of panel <tissue>_SV is the menu pair candidates[tissue]['pairs_s_v'][i] = (s, v) in line line_sidm[c[i]]; SV screen orientation = (anchor s, library v), verification orientation = (anchor v, library s); VS swaps them. The VS library must have identical a, b, c arrays (asserted).

part_A_reconciliation.step_1: Call the original followup_verification.policy_run (imported, unmodified) for every line x replicate x (static, feedback) x (screen_only, verify_hits, paired) with the same seed (line index) and sum per-line replicate means; must reproduce 3,958 / 3,762 measurements and 238.5 / 205.0 verified discoveries (and every other published total) exactly. The original results file and vault log are never written.
part_A_reconciliation.step_2: A faithful instrumented re-implementation of the original loop records every purchase; asserted equal to policy_run per line-replicate on all six returned fields.
part_A_reconciliation.step_3: Paired underuse per line: lost = M - 2 * sum_r floor(b_r / 2), b_r = min(ceil(M/4), M - spent). Unavoidable = M mod 2 (odd total with pair-only actions: at most 1 unit); avoidable = lost - unavoidable. Also per-round losses.
part_A_reconciliation.step_4: Original verify_hits: screen hits found in the final round and never verified, and how many of them would have validated (hidden).
part_A_reconciliation.step_5: Wells of the original arms: 14 x QC-passing plates (the frozen builder's charge) and 14 x design plates, by branch.

budget.measurement_version_primary: B = M = ceil(0.20 x menu size of the line) orientation measurements, identical for SV and VS. One orientation measurement (a pair-orientation in one line, with all its replicate plates in the release) costs 1 unit.
budget.physical_version_secondary: B = W = ceil(M x cbar) combination wells, cbar = mean over the line's menu of (c_screen + c_verify)/2, so W is identical for SV and VS and W = 14M when every orientation has one plate. A purchase costs c = 14 x design plates of that orientation in that line (7 library doses x 2 anchor concentrations per plate, every replicate plate charged, known before purchase; plates whose rows later fail QC are still paid). The builder's charge (14 x QC-passing plates) and the exported-row count (7 x design rows) are reported as alternative accountings.
budget.rounds: R = 4 decision rounds (as originally). Cumulative nominal capacity N_r = min(r x ceil(B/R), B).
budget.carry_over: Capacity available in round r = N_r - spent before round r: anything unused in a round carries forward to later rounds (including the terminal round).
budget.feasibility: Actions are taken greedily in the arm's priority order; an action that does not fit the remaining capacity is skipped and the next one tried. Measurement version: every arm spends exactly M, except paired which spends M - (M mod 2) (unavoidable remainder, at most 1 unit). Physical version: spend <= W; the final remainder is recorded and classed unavoidable if it is smaller than the cheapest still-available action of that arm, otherwise avoidable.
budget.result_timing: Purchases of a round are decided before any of that round's results are revealed; results arrive at the end of the round.

terminal_rule.rule: Arms that verify after screening (verify_hits_terminal, conf_per_cost, fixed_split, random and feedback with the verify-hits scheduler) get one verification-first terminal round R+1. In the last screening round R, screening is limited by a reserve sized from development history: candidates are accepted in priority order only while screen cost so far + c_s(i) + ceil(sum over accepted round-R screens of p_s(j) x c_v(j)) fits the capacity left after that round's verifications (p_s = history screen-call probability defined below; c = 1 in the measurement version). In round R+1 all capacity left (B - spent) first verifies unverified screen hits in the arm's verification order; any capacity still left is spent screening the next-ranked unscreened pairs ('terminal screens'), which cannot be verified inside the campaign and are reported separately. The extra round counts in elapsed time.
terminal_rule.fixed_split: Verification capacity B_v = floor(f x B) (physical: f x W) is reserved by construction; screening uses B_s = B - B_v in rounds 1..R (N_r^s = min(r x ceil(B_s/R), B_s), carry-over); round R+1 is the same verification-first terminal round (verify top screen hits by screen label with all remaining capacity, leftover to terminal screens).
terminal_rule.no_terminal_reference: verify_hits_noterminal = the original scheduler with exact spend (R rounds, verify first then screen; final-round hits stay unverified), kept as a reference for the terminal effect.

history_probabilities: For target line t in panel (tissue, replicate): history = all other lines of the same panel. Per pair: p_s = (n_screen_hit + k0 x base_s) / (n + k0); p_sv = (n_screen_and_valid + k0 x base_sv) / (n + k0); p_v_given_s = (n_screen_and_valid + k0 x base_v|s) / (n_screen_hit + k0); bases are pooled history rates of the panel; k0 = WorldConfig.shrink = 2.0. History lines' validation calls are history (the other orientation measured in other lines), never the target line's.

rankings.feedback: frozen Posterior(world).predict(screened, screen labels, 'full') on purchased screen labels only (verification labels are never fed, as originally); reference for the two main schedulers
rankings.random: agent.RandomArm(n, seed).scores, seeds 0..19, rng seed = seed (as in study.py); the zero arm for ranking
rankings.tie_break: np.lexsort((rng.random, -score)) as in agent._top; rng = default_rng(line index) for non-random arms

arms.screen_only: static ranking, R rounds, every unit screens; zero verification. Observed confirmed discoveries are 0 by the reporting rule; hidden validated screen hits are reported separately and are NOT zero biological hits.
arms.paired_full: static ranking; each purchase buys both orientations of the next-ranked pair in the same round (on different plates); per-round capacity with carry-over so total = M - (M mod 2); no terminal round.
arms.verify_hits_terminal: static ranking; every round first verifies earlier unverified screen hits (highest screen label first, as originally), then screens; reserve in round R; terminal round R+1.
arms.verify_hits_noterminal: reference: as above without reserve or terminal round (original scheduler, exact spend).
arms.fixed_split_dev: static ranking; two-stage fixed split with f selected on development units by leave-one-tissue-out (below).
arms.conf_per_cost: historical confirmation-probability-per-cost (static by construction): in every round the candidate actions are verify(unverified hit j) with value p_v_given_s(j)/c_v(j) and screen(new pair i) with value p_sv(i)/c_s(i) (c = 1 in the measurement version: cost is the price of the action being bought); greedy by value with fit; reserve in round R; terminal round verifies remaining hits by value, leftover to terminal screens by screen value. Ties broken by history_mean then the rng.
arms.random_verify_hits: random ranking (20 seeds) with the verify_hits_terminal scheduler; zero arm for ranking.
arms.time_sensitivity_secondary: static verify_hits_terminal with R = 1 and R = 2 screening rounds (elapsed 2 and 3 rounds); static screen_only, paired_full and fixed_split_dev with R = 1 to check that non-adaptive static arms do not need 4 rounds (outcomes reported, expected equal up to tie-breaks).

development_selection.rule: leave-one-tissue-out: for each tissue T, f*(T) = the grid value maximising total confirmed discoveries (line = mean of SV and VS) over the lines of the other two tissues under the static ranking; ties -> smaller f. Evaluated on T's lines. Selected separately in the measurement and physical versions. Rejected alternative: selecting on one swap replicate and evaluating on the other, because the SV validation call is the VS screen call of the same line (target-line leakage).
development_selection.disclosure: the full grid on every tissue (including the in-sample best f) is reported as a diagnostic only

endpoints.primary: independently confirmed discoveries actually obtained (screen call AND paid validation call), per line, summed over lines
secondary: first-screen yield (screen hits / screens; and screen hits total)
missed discoveries: hidden validated screen hits left unverified; validated pairs never screened
failures: purchased orientation measurements without QC-passing data (expected 0 by menu construction; verified) and replicate plates excluded by QC (design plates - QC-passing plates, a lower bound)
units/wells spent, unused capacity (avoidable vs unavoidable)
resources by branch and round under both plate models
rounds (scheduled, with purchases, minimum required by information flow) and minimum days
endpoints.diagnostic_only: confirmed discoveries per unit spent (labelled diagnostic; never a substitute for equal-budget comparison)

resource_accounting.per_purchase: orientation measurements (1), dose points (14 = 7 library doses x 2 anchor concentrations), combination wells (14 x design plates; also 14 x QC-passing plates and 7 x exported design rows), replicate plate-measurements
resource_accounting.plate_model_a_custom: 1536-well plate, one cell line per plate; 200 control wells per plate (6 untreated + 126 DMSO + 28 blank + 20 staurosporine + 20 MG-132, per the screening documentation); single agents 10 wells (5 reps x 2 conc) per distinct anchor drug and 28 wells (4 reps x 7 doses) per distinct library drug on that plate; combination 14 wells per orientation measurement per replicate. Packing per (arm, line x replicate, round, branch): replicate layer k (k = 1..max plates) holds every measurement with >= k replicate plates, so replicates never share a plate; within a layer first-fit in (library, anchor) order against 1536 - 200 wells. Branches are packed on separate plates (clean attribution; the two orientations of a pair never share a plate). Joint (branch-shared) packing per (line, round) with the same-pair conflict rule is reported as a diagnostic plate count.
resource_accounting.plate_model_b_native: a native Jaaks plate = one line x all anchors x one library doublet (design barcode). Buying a pair-orientation requires all its native plates (design barcodes for that line, anchor, library). Count distinct native plates touched per arm (attributed to the first round/branch that needs them), their combination wells (7 x design rows), single agents (10 per anchor + 28 per library drug on the plate), controls (200 per plate), and the fraction of their combination wells that belong to purchased orientations. Per-pair purchases are not physically separable in this layout; the other measurements on a touched plate are not credited.
resource_accounting.waiting: rounds; protocol minimum per round = 24 h attachment + 72 h drug exposure = 4 days; all other days (dispensing, readout, analysis, decision, culture expansion) unknown = null
unknown_null_with_reason: days beyond the 4-day protocol minimum per round
control and single-agent wells actually shared in a custom layout (model, not measured)
resource_accounting.computation: wall seconds per arm (perf_counter) and total

measurement_version.C4: feedback - static under the best scheduler; best = the one of {verify_hits_terminal, paired_full} with more static confirmed discoveries; the other scheduler's feedback contrast is also reported
measurement_version.C6: static verify_hits_terminal - static verify_hits_noterminal (terminal rule effect)

contrasts.physical_version: the same six contrasts with wells budgets

inference: research.astra.feedback_validation_20261003.verdict.contrast (paired line differences, stratified percentile bootstrap by tissue, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261003; relative gain = ratio of sums). Exploratory: intervals are descriptive, no multiplicity adjustment, no verdict categories.
stopping_rule: one replay execution with this plan; no sequential looks and no re-running with changed rules after outcomes are seen. A bug fix after outcomes are read is allowed only if a test exposes it; it is recorded in receipts/deviations.json with before/after values. Any new analysis after outcomes gets an addendum, not a plan edit.
tests: allocation/test_allocation.py on synthetic data only (no Jaaks outcomes): budget conservation (exact spend, paired remainder <= 1, carry-over, physical remainder classed), terminal verification of final-round hits, legal access (unpurchased labels never change purchases; validation labels never change any purchase), condition identity (verification = other orientation of the same pair in the same line, disjoint barcodes).

outputs.results/replay.json: per-arm tables (both versions), contrasts, fixed-split grid, time sensitivity
outputs.receipts/accounting.json: resource accounting by arm, branch and round under both plate models, failures, waiting, computation, unknowns
outputs.receipts/deviations.json: deviations from this plan and from the coordinator brief
outputs.results/lines.jsonl: per line x replicate x arm records
